Save MODGEE results as CSV and RDS files

Source: R/save_result.R
save_result.Rd

Export existing estimates without refitting or recomputing intervals.

Usage

save_result(result, path = ".", prefix = "modgee", overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

result

A complete result returned by fit_modgee().

path

Output directory, created recursively if needed. Defaults to the current working directory.

prefix

Filename prefix. An underscore is appended unless the prefix is empty or already ends with one. Defaults to "modgee".

overwrite

Allow replacement of existing target files. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

Writes three to five CSV files and one RDS file to path. Each filename starts with prefix followed by an underscore; an empty prefix adds nothing. For example, prefix = "hk" produces hk_summary.csv and, when bootstrap results are available, hk_CI.csv.

CSV files

summary.csv

One overall row, followed by one row per supplied group when groups are present. Columns scope ("overall" or "group") and group identify the rows; the overall group label is NA. The remaining overall columns are baseline_timestep, final_timestep, excluded_species, known_species, singleton_species, known_extant, known_extinct, dark_extinct, total_extinct, original_richness, cumulative_extinction_rate and AIC, copied from result$summary. Group rows contain the corresponding group estimates. With groups, l is also included: it is the group's hazard multiplier, with 1 for the reference group and NA for the overall row and unfitted groups. AIC is an overall model statistic and is NA on group rows. Groups containing only all-zero species remain in this table, with undefined estimates as NA.

time_result.csv

A long-format table: one row per time step for the overall model, followed by one row per time step for each fitted group. Columns are scope, group, time, h, m and cumulative_extinction_rate. The overall rows contain the shared survey parameter h, the reference hazard m and the overall cumulative extinction rate. Group rows contain their own hazard m and cumulative extinction rate; their h is NA because the shared value is already recorded in the overall rows. Time labels are copied from the fitted result.

species_result.csv

One row per input species, in the original input order. Copies result$species, including species, belonged_group (when grouped), detected_timesteps, is_singleton, first_detection_timestep, last_detection_timestep, d, p_extinct and estimated_extinction_year. All-zero species are retained with NA estimates. The extinction year is conditional on extinction, as defined in fit_modgee.

k_comparison.csv

Written only when result$do_k is not NULL. Copies that table: fixed-k and free-k model rows, with model, k, group multipliers l_<group> when present, AIC and converged. No new models are fitted.

CI.csv

Written only when result$bootstrap is not NULL. Combines result$bootstrap$curve and, when present, result$bootstrap$group_results$curve. Overall rows come first, followed by group rows. Columns scope, group and time identify each curve point. estimate is the original fitted cumulative extinction rate; lower and upper are its pointwise bootstrap confidence limits at the confidence level used in fit_modgee(). n_valid is the number of valid bootstrap estimates used for that point. Undefined limits remain NA. Only curve intervals are exported, not intervals for summary metrics, parameters or individual species.

Details

Always writes summary.csv, time_result.csv and species_result.csv, with the requested prefix. Summary and time tables contain overall rows first, followed by group rows. The scope column is "overall" or "group"; group is NA for overall rows, so a real group named "overall" remains unambiguous. Missing columns are filled with NA. Group summaries retain l; their AIC is NA. Group time rows contain the group's own m and cumulative extinction rate; h is NA because h is shared and recorded on overall rows only. All-zero-only groups remain in summary but have no fitted curve rows. Species results retain all input rows, columns and their original order.

If result$do_k is non-NULL, k_comparison.csv contains that table unchanged apart from omission of row names. If result$bootstrap is non-NULL, CI.csv combines bootstrap$curve and bootstrap$group_results$curve, with scope and group columns. These are pointwise cumulative-extinction intervals: time, estimate, lower, upper and n_valid. No summary-metric intervals or replicate tables are exported to CSV.

CSV files use UTF-8, comma separators, NA for missing values and no row numbers. Estimates are not rounded, clipped or recomputed. All tables and filename conflicts are checked before writing. All files are staged before installation; a failed installation attempts to restore previous files. This is not a concurrent-writer transaction; use a separate directory for simultaneous exports. Optional files left by earlier calls are not deleted; use distinct prefixes for different analyses. The prefixed result.rds file preserves the complete R object, including diagnostics and bootstrap information.

Usage Examples


# Save ungrouped results.
save_result(example_result, path = "results")

# Save grouped results.
save_result(example_grouped_result, path = "results", prefix = "grouped")

# Save bootstrap results.
save_result(example_bootstrap_result, path = "results", prefix = "bootstrap")

See also

Functions: read_matrix, fit_modgee, plot_modgee

Examples: example_file, example_M, example_groups, example_result, example_grouped_result, example_bootstrap_result

Complete R object

The RDS filename is modgee_result.rds with the default prefix, hk_result.rds with prefix = "hk", or result.rds with an empty prefix. Restore the complete object with readRDS(). RDS exports use the same overwrite checks, staging and rollback as CSV files. The function invisibly returns a data frame with columns table, file, nrow and ncol. The RDS row has table = "result" and NA for both dimensions.
